filename: Toward a Climate OSSE Framework for Satellite Mission Design.pdf
title: Toward a Climate OSSE Framework for Satellite Mission Design
venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
parameterization_target: atmospheric physics parameters (cumulus entrainment, relaxation time, critical RH, snow fall speed, autoconversion)
testbed_rationale: The archived data contains summary posterior parameter distributions, net cloud feedback, and ECS estimates for figure reproduction rather than training/evaluation data for developing ML parameterizations.
pain_points: Computational expense of high-dimensional MCMC sampling for climate models requires surrogate ML emulators
Poor characterization of observational uncertainties in satellite retrievals (e.g., cloudy boundary layer thermodynamic state) widens posterior parameter spread
Distinguishing model structural error from parametric error: parameter tuning cannot fix structural parameterization shortcomings
Representativeness error and lack of spatial/temporal sampling homogeneity in satellite observations
Absence of an established climate OSSE framework linking prospective satellite observing systems to climate projection uncertainty metrics
extraction_notes: Acknowledges support from NSF STC Learning the Earth with Artificial Intelligence and Physics (LEAP, NSF Award 2019625). The ML emulator and GISS-E3 CPE framework are introduced in Elsaesser et al. (2025) and applied here as a climate OSSE proof of concept.
